comments.body: What is this issue? Just for adding `[MODIFIED]` label and should be already closed or I totally miss the point? :)

Preloading is a separate issue described here: https://hstspreload.org/ - This is a specialized portion of the HSTS standard to allow your site to be _preloaded in browser software_ so its just not possible to even try to make a HTTP request to a site, even before you visit the site and get a HSTS response header (hence, pre-loading).

I propose to cite **HSTS** as a control for PCI-DSS v3.2.1 Requirements from Issue https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/issues/317#issuecomment-829077114:

- [2.2.3](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/136826/116527891-81febb00-a91e-11eb-9bce-5441194ced91.png)
- [2.3](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/136826/116528176-d99d2680-a91e-11eb-93a8-4799d302ec47.png)

I propose to cite HSTS **Preloading** as a control for [PCI-DSS v3.2.1 Requirement 4.1](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/136826/116528344-1406c380-a91f-11eb-8816-3bc5712d97ce.png)

Can @jmanico and/or @tghosth and/or other Project Manager(s) approve the above so I can create the Pull Request(s) or instruct me to create a related new issue to https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/issues/317#issuecomment-829077114

At the moment personally I can not understand, what is your proposal. I share my "template" what I have used sometimes:
```
Proposal:
* [Label](https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md): todo
* Category: todo
  * todo: no changes or why it changes
* Id: todo
  * todo: no changes or why it changes
* Requirement: todo
  * todo: no changes or why it changes
* Levels: todo
  * todo: no changes or why it changes
* NIST: todo
  * todo: for some V2 and V3 requirements
* CWE: todo
  * todo: comments if needed
```

> At the moment personally I can not understand, what is your proposal. I share my "template" what I have used sometimes:

Can I reuse this as [template for issues](https://docs.github.com/en/communities/using-templates-to-encourage-useful-issues-and-pull-requests/configuring-issue-templates-for-your-repository) with credit to you @elarlang ?

https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/issues/966#issuecomment-833353752 is to support the modification of [Appendix D of ASVS v3.0](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/136826/50191893-0b337980-0384-11e9-9781-ddc35239a7b8.png) and insertion into  [ASVS 4.1](https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/issues/317#issuecomment-797796017) . 

Please let me know if I need to [create a new but related issue](https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/issues/new/choose) to #317 (comment)?

## offtopic - issue template

You can use this template wherever you want :) At the moment, till we don't have clear development process written anywhere, this template should be "all discussions in issues should reach to that proposal (template)". Not sure it works as intended as independent template without having process and expectation in place. Current issue template can be improved, I agree.

## on topic

Current issue is spin-off from #963, and as I understand, direction is to make separate "Level 3" requirement additionally for current 14.4.5 with recommending using "preload".

Maybe I didn't investigate enough all the links you provided, but I'm not sure those are all related. That's why I shared my template - with that structure it is clear from ASVS point of view, what kind of change you propose.

This was covered in [ASVS v3.0.1-10.12](https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/master/3.0.1/ASVS-excel-v3.0.1.xlsx)
> Verify that production website URL has been submitted to preloaded list of Strict Transport Security domains maintained by web browser vendors. Please see the references below.

(Not recommending to use it as it is)

I support a level 3 requirement around HSTS preloading, but I prefer not to add PCI-DSS text in it. PCI-DSS does not discuss preloading at all. So @cmlh if you want to take a stab at this requirement, please give it a run here in the issue tracker first. I do not think we need PCI citations attached to the requirement though.

[PCI-DSS v3.2.1 Requirement 4.1](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/136826/116528344-1406c380-a91f-11eb-8816-3bc5712d97ce.png) states  "_Only trusted keys and certificates are accepted_." which is the same control enforced by Preloading. 

I have marked HSTS as the control for PCI-DSS v3.2.1 Requirements [2.2.3](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/136826/116527891-81febb00-a91e-11eb-9bce-5441194ced91.png) and [2.3](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/136826/116528176-d99d2680-a91e-11eb-93a8-4799d302ec47.png) within the Markdown Task List at the end of Issue https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/issues/317#issuecomment-829077114

Would @jmanico support that I forked ASVS to support PCI-DSS v3.2.1?

> "_Only trusted keys and certificates are accepted_." which is the same control enforced by Preloading.

Extra parameter `preload` in `Strict-Transport-Security` headers sets limitation to browser, that domains in "preload" list can be accessed only using HTTPS connection. That's it. Nothing about certificates.

> Extra parameter `preload` in `Strict-Transport-Security` headers sets limitation to browser, that domains in "preload" list can be accessed only using HTTPS connection. That's it. Nothing about certificates.

The preloaded https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/master:net/http/transport_security_state_static.json lists the `pinsets` of trusted certificates.

To force browsers using / to get effect from "preload" attribute, your domain must have valid certificate first. From that perspective I can understand your quote "Only trusted keys and certificates are accepted".

Scope for the issue is `Strict-Transport-Security` response header. Valid certificates are required by V9.1.* requirements and those are required also without "preload" attribute in `Strict-Transport-Security` header. Look them separately.

Therefore I repeat my recommendation in https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/issues/966#issuecomment-833359450 . Please write proposal in "ASVS format". If you through a lot of links and some out of context piece of information, it's complicated to understand, what is your message or what is your proposal.

Or other option in this case - you can see, that this requirement will be in place in the future, just follow the issue to see, how and when it happens.

I don't believe @elarlang Issue Template would be applicable in this case as I consider my matter closed as @jmanico responded with https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/issues/966#issuecomment-833615779 below

> I do not think we need PCI citations attached to the requirement though.

I therefore intend to proceed with https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/issues/966#issuecomment-833960359

> Would @jmanico support that I forked ASVS to support PCI-DSS v3.2.1?

Please don't let this discourage @elarlang from pursing the [Issue's Template](https://docs.github.com/en/communities/using-templates-to-encourage-useful-issues-and-pull-requests/configuring-issue-templates-for-your-repository)

Alternative for adding new requirement, it's possible to use solution like it's done with [3.3.2](https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/master/4.0/en/0x12-V3-Session-management.md)

`+` It does not feel like duplicate requirement, which may be confusing
`-` it is maybe not that clear to read from requirement text alone.
Preloading is a little bit too deep for now, so closing this out.

`2.2 HTTPS-only`
`Redirect traffic from HTTP protocol (port 80) to HTTPS (port 443)`
